text:
Relevant evidence spans foundational work and a recent 2026 preprint. [Gu et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/gu20a.html) explain that long-memory gates approach saturation, preserving information while making gate learning difficult; saturation alone therefore does not establish forgetting. A [2026 controlled LSTM/GRU study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29034) measures final-hidden-state sensitivity at each input lag while varying gate initialization and recurrent regularization. Its synthetic-task results concern optimization, explicitly not finite-sample generalization. [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073) provides event-level perturbation attribution and history pruning, but explains output dependence rather than locating where recurrent information disappears.

Suggested synthesis for GRU4Rec: freeze a target and competitor, then attribute their score margin m=s(target)−s(competitor). At selected nonpadding lags, compare input-to-final-state sensitivity with input-to-margin gradients. Perturb an intermediate hidden state by a small, norm-bounded vector, replay the unchanged suffix, and measure both final-state displacement and margin change. Attenuated state displacement supports local recurrent contraction; surviving displacement with negligible margin change supports output insensitivity along that direction. These are proposed diagnostics, not established findings for this benchmark.

Validate directional derivatives against central finite differences at several step sizes; disable dropout and require a zero-intervention replay to reproduce baseline states and scores. Keep competitor identities fixed during differentiation, exclude padding, and report signed effects plus magnitudes to expose cancellation. [Captum’s infidelity metric](https://captum.ai/api/metrics.html) formalizes checking attribution-predicted changes against measured perturbation effects. Small gradients can reflect local saturation, and large interventions can leave the normal state distribution. Neither probe establishes current intent or generalization; predictive benefit still requires the fixed validation HR@10 evaluation.
